explanation: No SEBI-registered adviser or broker may promise guaranteed or assured returns on market investments. Anyone who does is either unregistered or lying.
legal_basis: SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations 2013; SEBI (PFUTP) Regulations 2003, Reg 3 & 4

explanation: A fixed monthly payout from stock market investment is not a legal product in India. This is the standard structure of a Ponzi scheme.
legal_basis: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act 2019; SEBI (PFUTP) Regulations 2003

explanation: Equity and derivatives carry market risk by definition. A risk-free equity return is a contradiction, not a product.
Promises of doubling money in a fixed period are the signature of investment fraud. No legitimate market product works this way.
IPO allotment in an oversubscribed issue is decided by a computerised lottery run by the registrar. Nobody can guarantee you an allotment.
Exclusive or guaranteed pre-IPO allotments sold over chat are almost always fake. Genuine pre-IPO transfers happen through a demat account with a documented contract.
Retail forex and binary options trading on overseas electronic platforms is prohibited for Indian residents. There is no recovery route if you lose money there.
legal_basis: FEMA 1999; RBI Alert List of unauthorised forex platforms

explanation: Being asked to pay a fee before you can withdraw your own money is the defining move of a fake trading app. Real brokers deduct charges from the payout; they never ask you to send money first.
Your withdrawal is blocked until you pay something. This is how fake investment apps extract a second round of money from victims.
Investment money must go to the intermediary's own designated bank account, never to an individual's personal UPI or account. This is the single clearest sign of fraud.
legal_basis: SEBI circular on UPI mechanism for registered intermediaries (effective 01 Oct 2025)

explanation: Letting someone route money through your bank account makes you a mule account holder. That is a criminal offence and your account will be frozen.
A charge to reactivate your own account is not a real product. Brokers reactivate dormant accounts through re-KYC, not payment.
No genuine institution ever asks for an OTP, PIN, CVV or password. Anyone requesting one is attempting to take money from your account.
legal_basis: RBI customer protection circulars; BNS 2023 s.318

explanation: Installing a screen-sharing app at a stranger's request hands them live control of your banking and demat sessions. No legitimate support process requires this.
Genuine broking and mutual fund apps are distributed only through the Play Store or App Store. An APK sent to you is how fake trading apps get installed.
legal_basis: SEBI investor advisories on unauthorised trading apps

explanation: Regulators and exchanges never contact individual investors to demand payment. Any message that does is an impersonation attempt.
There is no such legal procedure as a digital arrest anywhere in Indian law. Police and central agencies do not interrogate people over video calls or demand money to close a case.
legal_basis: BNS 2023 s.204, s.308; MHA cybercrime advisories

explanation: SEBI registers intermediaries; it never approves, certifies or guarantees an investment scheme or its returns. Any claim that SEBI backs a return is false.
legal_basis: SEBI Act 1992; SEBI investor caution list

explanation: Acting on genuine insider information is a criminal offence, and claims of having it are usually bait. Either way, do not engage.
You cannot win a lottery you never entered. The prize is bait for the processing fee they will ask for next.
legal_basis: BNS 2023 s.318; Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act 1978

explanation: Messages claiming your demat account is frozen are designed to panic you into acting. Check the status by logging into your broker directly, never through a link in a message.
Urgent KYC-expiry messages with a deadline and a link are a standard phishing template. Regulated entities give notice through your registered contact and their own app.
Unclaimed dividends are genuinely common in India, which is exactly why fraudsters use this hook. Real unclaimed amounts are claimed through the registrar or IEPF, never through a link.
legal_basis: Companies Act 2013 s.124-125; SEBI circulars on unclaimed amounts

explanation: Artificial time pressure is used to stop you from checking. A genuine investment opportunity survives you taking a day to verify it.
Paid VIP stock-tip groups are the most common entry point into securities fraud. Registered advisers do not run anonymous tip groups.
Investment advice delivered through an anonymous chat group has no regulatory accountability. You cannot complain to SEBI about someone you cannot identify.
Handing account control to someone for a share of profits is unregistered portfolio management. If they lose your money you have no regulatory recourse.
Every regulated investment in India requires KYC and PAN. An offer that skips them is outside the regulated system entirely.
